title: CNSAS Piemonte drone imagery analyzed with AI software, likely TEXSAR's ADIAT, locates missing surgeon Nicola Ivaldo on Monviso after ten months
summary: AI analysis of 2,600 drone frames flagged a red helmet in the Perotti couloir at 3,150 m; Ivaldo's body was recovered by 31 July 2025.
account: Nicola Ivaldo, a surgeon aged 64 according to the Club Alpino Italiano's Lo Scarpone (another report says 66), disappeared on 14 September 2024 per CAI (Quadricottero dates his departure, when he parked his car at the Pontechianale dam, to 15 September) during a solo outing on Monviso in Piedmont, Italy; searches over ten months found nothing. On 29 July 2025 the Soccorso Alpino e Speleologico Piemontese (CNSAS) flew two drones close to the north face, collecting about 2,600 high-resolution frames over 183 hectares in five hours. Analyzed pixel by pixel with AI image-analysis software, identified by its developer TEXSAR as the open-source Automated Drone Image Analysis Tool (ADIAT), the frames yielded a tiny red anomaly in the Perotti couloir: his helmet. His body was located at about 3,150 m and recovered by 31 July 2025; that date comes from TEXSAR's page (which cites Wired) and is consistent with bluewin's report of under 72 hours from the 29 July flight to the recovery, while CAI gives only July 2025 and Quadricottero no date.
purpose: ADIAT was built to scan drone photographs and flag color and shape anomalies for search-and-rescue teams; locating the missing man's helmet was that intended function.
system: AI drone-image analysis software used by CNSAS Piemonte (identified as ADIAT by its developer, TEXSAR; CAI and CNSAS sources do not name it)
developer: TEXSAR (Texas Search and Rescue) volunteers, per the developer's own account
deployer: Soccorso Alpino e Speleologico Piemontese (CNSAS Piemonte), Turin station drone team
location: Monviso north face, Perotti couloir (province of Cuneo), Italy
segment: Recovery of a missing person in high-alpine terrain
taxonomy_note: The time cut is the rescuers' frame review; the family's good, recovery of remains, has no type.

ratings.reason: Ivaldo's family obtained recovery of his body and certainty about his fate after ten months of searching; a material benefit, not life-saving, since he had died in September 2024.

CNSAS Piemonte ended a search that had involved ground teams, Guardia di Finanza and fire-service helicopters for ten months; manual analysis of the drone photos would have taken weeks (CAI) to months (CNSAS, per bluewin).

ai_role.statement: The AI flagged a few red pixels, the helmet, a detail CAI describes as invisible to the naked eye, in a search that ten months of helicopters, specialist teams and advanced technology (Quadricottero) had not resolved; drone pilot Saverio Isola is quoted that it was the AI software that identified the differently colored pixels. CAI/CNSAS sources do not name the software; the ADIAT attribution comes from the developer TEXSAR's own page, so the tool identity rests on a vendor-authored source.

produced_by: Close-range high-resolution drone photography of steep faces (about 2,600 frames over 183 hectares)
A target object (red helmet) with strong color contrast against rock and ice
Search area narrowed by mobile-phone cell data to the Monviso and Visolotto faces
must_hold: Weather and terrain allow drones to fly close to the walls
The subject or equipment remains visible and not buried by snow
Rescuers verify AI flags, which CNSAS notes can also fire on plastic or unusual rock color

headline: ADIAT spots a red helmet and locates Nicola Ivaldo on Monviso
metric: located at about 3,150 m and recovered by 31 July 2025

comparator.against: conventional ground and air searches over the preceding months
comparator.before: I metodi di ricerca convenzionali sono rimasti inconcludenti per mesi
comparator.after: meno di 72 ore dalla prima missione del drone al recupero del corpo
comparator.quote: I metodi di ricerca convenzionali sono rimasti inconcludenti per mesi, mentre sono passate meno di 72 ore dalla prima missione del drone al recupero del corpo.

later.note: By January 2026 the CNSAS Piemonte drone lead was working with Politecnico di Torino's geomatics team on a successor tool that adds precise georeferenced coordinates to the color-anomaly detection.
later.quote: Giordan, che è anche soccorritore, sta collaborando con il team di geomatica del Politecnico di Torino per sviluppare un software capace non solo di individuare anomalie cromatiche, ma di fornire coordinate georeferenziate di estrema precisione.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.

Corrected the bluewin.ch title to the page's headline, hedged the title's ADIAT attribution to its vendor source, placed the find on the Monviso north face rather than at Pontechianale (only his starting point), removed the unsupported claim that human reviewers had missed the helmet, and noted that the sources differ on the manual-review time (weeks per CAI, months per CNSAS via bluewin), the disappearance date (14 or 15 September 2024) and the source of the 31 July 2025 recovery date.
Merged with a second write-up of the same event (11 sources and the registry id carried over); the duplicate was removed.
Title reworded to state the event without naming who claims it.
Added what the benefit is measured against, what happened since from the cited sources.
Benefit type set to Reduced Task Time under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Organizational Efficiency among the six first used.

claim_basis: 11 independent news reports, one other independent source, the makers' press release and two press releases from the deployer are on file. There is no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
